promise: See how an event lets one service hand work to independent consumers without making the user wait.

sections.heading: Synchronous versus event-driven
sections.body_markdown: Direct calls are simple, but they couple the caller to every dependency. The caller waits while each API runs, and one slow API can fail the whole request. An event flips that: the app records what happened, returns, and consumers work later. Publishers do not know who consumes the event, so one slow consumer cannot block the publisher.

rows: Only until the event is stored
One slow API fails the request

sections.heading: The registration flow
sections.body_markdown: A new user submits the registration form. The app saves the user and publishes an event. An email worker sends the welcome message, then a CRM worker creates the marketing profile. The request returns before either worker finishes. Consumers can retry independently.

items.title: Accept the request
items.text: The form is saved and the request returns immediately.

items.title: Publish the event
items.text: The `user_registered` event carries the new user id.

items.title: Work in the background
items.text: Subscribed workers pick up the event and retry on failure.

sections.heading: Choose the simplest tool
sections.body_markdown: A plain background task fits a quick one-off job. A stateful process fits work that needs shared state. A pub/sub topic fits one event with many unknown subscribers. Keep the user-facing path synchronous only where the answer is required.

items.title: Background task
items.text: Fits one quick job, such as sending a single email.

items.title: Pub/sub topic
items.text: Fits one event with many unknown subscribers.

assignment: Map one synchronous flow in an app you use. List which steps could move behind an event and which must stay synchronous.

questions.prompt: What does a publisher know about its consumers?
options: Publishers do not know who consumes the event
Every consumer must register its address with the publisher
The publisher calls each consumer one at a time
The publisher waits for every consumer to reply
questions.explanation: Publishers do not know who consumes the event, so consumers can subscribe without changing the publisher.

questions.prompt: An event-driven request can return before the welcome email is sent.
questions.explanation: The request returns once the event is stored; the email worker handles the message later.

questions.prompt: Which are benefits of event-driven registration?
options: One slow consumer cannot block the publisher
The publisher must know every consumer
The request waits for every consumer to reply
questions.explanation: Independent consumers can fail or retry without holding up the publisher, and background work smooths out spikes.

questions.prompt: Put the event-driven registration steps in order.
items: App saves the user and publishes an event
Email worker sends the welcome message
CRM worker creates the marketing profile
questions.explanation: The app publishes after saving, and the independent workers consume the event afterward.
